content.text: `alinea/server` runs Alinea in any Node server that works with web `Request` and `Response` objects, such as Hono, and in scripts and static site generators. The framework integrations are built on it.
Create the CMS
Create your CMS with `createCMS` from `alinea/server`. `baseUrl` is where your site runs, `handlerUrl` the route of the Alinea API and `adminPath` the path of the dashboard:
Add the middleware

`createMiddleware(cms)` returns a function that takes a request and a `next` function that renders your site. It answers the Alinea routes itself and runs `next` for everything else. Put it in front of your app, here a Hono app served by `@hono/node-server`:
For every request the middleware:
proxies the dashboard to the Alinea CLI during development,
answers the handler route, `GET` requests for media files under `/admin/file/` and the dashboard route `/admin` itself,
otherwise renders your page within the request, so queries see drafts when an editor previews the page.
Pass options instead of the CMS to configure the handler, for example a custom
backend
or hooks, and the previews:

Express and `node:http` servers do not use web requests. Adapt them with `getRequestListener` from `@hono/node-server`, which turns a function from `Request` to `Response` into a Node request listener. In an Express app, answer the Alinea routes with `createHandler(cms)` and wrap your route handlers in `withRequest` (below) so queries see drafts.
Queries outside the middleware
Queries run by the middleware's `next` know which request they belong to. Code that renders outside of it, like a custom route or a static site generator, passes the request with `withRequest`:
Scripts and builds that do not serve requests can query `cms` directly. They only see published content.
Live previews

The dashboard previews an entry by loading its page with a preview token. The handler turns that into a signed draft cookie and redirects to the page. The middleware then adds a small script to the HTML of draft pages, which receives the edits from the dashboard and reloads the page while keeping its scroll position. With `previews: {widget: true}` the page also shows the floating preview toolbar. Set `previews: false` to leave draft pages untouched.
Sites that can refresh without a full reload listen for the `alinea:refresh` event, cancel it and call `done` once the new content is rendered:
Develop and build
Run your server through the Alinea CLI. It generates your content database, starts the dashboard and passes its location to your server in environment variables:

Open `http://localhost:3000/admin` to edit content. `alinea build` writes the production dashboard into your public folder and generates the content database. If your site has a build step of its own, pass it after `--` like in development. Serve the public folder as static files: the middleware redirects `/admin` to the dashboard in it.
Deploy
Your server needs a Node runtime: pages query the SQLite database generated in `@alinea/generated`, so deploy `node_modules` (or trace it along) with your build.
Set `ALINEA_API_KEY` in the production environment. The handler uses it to sign preview tokens and draft cookies, and to talk to its backend.
The handler saves edits as commits through
Alinea Cloud or your own backend
. Running servers sync their database with the handler, so published changes show without a redeploy.
